newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian party cancels campaign in protest.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian party cancels campaign in protest.

text.p: Indonesia's Moslem-oriented minority party said it had cancelled election rallies in Jakarta on Friday to protest the refusal by police to grant permission for a meeting.

"Police have refused to grant permission for a gathering in south Jakarta today which will be attended by (party chairman) Ismail Hasan Metareum. There has been no reason given for the refusal," Amin Sannang, a spokesman for the United Development Party (PPP), said by telephone.

"It's them (the police) who, in fact, have disturbed the election. What is the reason for not giving the permit? Are there houses or shops which have been burned because of the PPP campaign?" he said.
Police spokesmen were not available for comment.

Only the PPP, the ruling Golkar and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are allowed to contest the national parliamentary elections on May 29, and they need police permission to hold campaign rallies.
At stake are 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives. Another 75 seats are allotted to the military, which does not vote. The campaign will last through May 23.

The PPP had planned to hold campaign rallies at five places in Jakarta on Friday but has cancelled them. It has scheduled rallies in several cities on Java island, Moluccas and remote Irian Jaya province in the western half of New Guinea island.
Metareum was not available for comment, but Sannang said the chairman was aware of the campaigning boycott in Jakarta.
The PPP had earlier decided to cancel campaigning in Yogyakarta city in Central Java after a group of people smashed the windows of the party's office on Wednesday.
The Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Friday that local PPP supporters lowered the party's flags and removed signs and posters that had been erected for its campaign.
Sannang confirmed the reports and said whether the party would continue its campaign in Yogyakarta would depend on further negotiations. He gave no further details.
The official Antara news agency reported on Friday that police in Pekalongan, central Java, had detained eight people after a clash involving supporters of rival parties on Wednesday.
Residents in Pekalongan, a PPP stronghold, earlier said 18 people were injured when supporters of Golkar and PPP clashed. The PPP is scheduled to hold a campaign on Friday in Pekalongan.

The town, on the coast in Central Java, has been the site of clashes since March between supporters of the PPP and Golkar. The ruling party is seeking to push its share of votes above 70 percent after winning 68 percent at the last election in 1992.
Tensions have risen since the start last Sunday of the campaign for the elections, and there have been minor clashes between Golkar and PPP supporters elsewhere in the country.
